newsitem.title: USA: Pinnacle to unveil consumer editing unit.
newsitem.headline: Pinnacle to unveil consumer editing unit.

text.p: Pinnacle Systems Inc on Monday will unveil a video-editing device for home movie makers in a move to expand into the growing consumer market, company executives said.

The $295 unit, which will be sold through computer stores starting January, connects to a personal computer and camcorder. With editing software included with the unit, amature Spielbergs can then edit scenes, reshuffle their order and add special effects. The unit transfers the finished production to a regular VHS tape.

The VideoDirector Studio 200 is part of Pinnacle's efforts to tap the emerging consumer market for gadgets that can edit photos and videos on home PCs, a market that could be as big as $1 billion in a few years, said Bill Loesch, Pinnacle vice president of consumer products group.
"This is going to be a very significant fraction of our revenue," Loesch said Friday.
Pinnacle, based in Sunnyvale, Calif., makes electronic devices and software that let broadcasters create special effects, animated logos and graphics for television.
Until now, only professional editors and studios could afford Pinnacle's products, which costs as much as $100,000.

Loesch said as personal computers appear in more homes, more people can do digital video editing. The growing acceptance of photo-editing products also is a sign that the market for home video editing is about to take off, he said.
Loesch declined to forecast the impact of the product to Pinnacle's sales, but said it will be "substantial."

In recent months, Pinnacle's stock has been battered amid slowing revenue growth, marketing missteps and higher costs. The stock has plunged about 70 percent from a high of 35 1/2 last November. On Friday, the stock closed down 3/4 at 9 7/8.
